The new GET /agents/{system_id}/dhcp-data endpoint follows the existing internal-API handler/response patterns: the service method exists and is wired into ServiceCollectionV3 (maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py:118, services/__init__.py:279,658), and the 404/422 mappings are handled by ExceptionMiddleware (maasapiserver/common/middlewares/exceptions.py), so the documented responses match runtime behavior. The test fixture app includes both RequireClientCertMiddleware and ExceptionMiddleware, so the 403/404/422 tests exercise the real middleware chain. Main concern is authorization: the path system_id is never bound to the authenticated client certificate, so any enrolled agent can fetch any rack's DHCP data (see inline). Secondary design note: the response schema embeds the service-layer stdlib dataclasses directly, making internal structs the wire contract. Drive-by pre-existing bug worth fixing while in this file: AgentConfigResponse.kind defaults to "AgentSignedCertificate" (src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models/responses/agent.py:45) — a copy-paste from the certificate response; the config response should default to "AgentConfig".

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.212: Security: `system_id` is taken directly from the URL and never checked against the authenticated caller. RequireClientCertMiddleware only verifies that a client certificate is present — the CN (the agent UUID, set at enrollment in enroll_agent) is stored in `request.scope["client_cn"]` but is not compared with the path parameter here. As written, any enrolled agent can retrieve the full DHCP configuration of any other rack controller: subnets, dynamic pools, and reserved IPs with MAC addresses and hostnames — a full network-topology disclosure from one compromised rack. Consider resolving the agent from the cert CN and verifying it maps to the requested rack (or deriving the system_id from the authenticated agent and ignoring the path parameter).

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models.73: These fields are the stdlib `@dataclass` types from maasservicelayer.models.dhcp, so the agent-facing wire schema is now defined by internal service-layer structs rather than dedicated Pydantic response models (service-layer models in this codebase are otherwise Pydantic BaseModels; plain dataclasses are the exception). Pydantic v2 does support stdlib dataclasses as field types for validation, JSON-schema generation and serialization, so this works, but any field rename or addition in those dataclasses now silently changes the agent API contract with no alias or versioning boundary. If the dataclasses are intended to be the wire contract, that's fine — otherwise consider dedicated response models here.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.402: Unlike the neighboring 404/503 tests (e.g. test_agent_config_404 asserts details[0]["type"] and details[0]["message"]), this test (and test_agent_dhcp_data_422_when_rack_not_configured below) only asserts the status code. Consider also asserting the error body matches the documented NotFoundBodyResponse/ValidationErrorBodyResponse shape — particularly that the ValidationException details carry the expected field/message ("The rack controller has no current configuration.") — so a regression in the ExceptionMiddleware mapping or in build_for_field would be caught.
